name: clear_bit_in_row_pairs
description: Walks a table of 40 row pointers and clears bit six in each addressed byte and in the byte 40 bytes further on, updating both bitplanes of each row pair.

name: set_pixel_bit_in_planes
description: Computes the byte and bit position of a pixel from its x and y coordinates on an 80-byte-stride bitplane, stores both in an output record, then sets that bit in one plane, both planes, or the second plane only, depending on the colour value.

name: store_row_address_pairs
description: Writes a starting address into two table slots, splitting each 32-bit value into high and low words, and advances the address by 40 bytes between the slots.

name: repeat_call_routine_eleven_times
description: Invokes one other routine eleven times in a row with no arguments and returns, with no other work in the body.

name: clear_state_and_run_steps
description: Clears one global flag, stores a fixed value into a second global, and interleaves those writes with calls to other routines.

name: set_state_and_run_steps
description: Sets one global to one and another global to a fixed value, with a further constant stored into a third global, interleaved with calls to other routines.

name: unpack_multiplane_graphics_into_buffers
description: Copies word-sized tiles from a graphics table into interleaved plane buffers, then copies bytes and longwords from the same table into other buffers. The referenced files BIGCHAR.IFF and PANEL.SPR show which graphics are unpacked.

name: select_indexed_entry_then_load
description: Reads a 32-bit entry from a table indexed by a word value and passes it to a loader routine; when the entry is not minus one, it repeats the load with a second value and calls further routines.

name: select_indexed_entry_then_call
description: Looks up a 32-bit entry in a table using a word index, stores it in a global, then calls one routine with a fixed reference value.

name: request_arthur_sprite_load
description: Zeroes one global, points two others at a shared buffer and a loader routine, calls the loader, adds a value read from a fixed memory location, and calls it again. The referenced file ARTHUR1.SPR is the sprite being requested.

name: request_weapons_sprite_files
description: Sets a fixed value and a shared buffer pointer, calls the loader, then resets the buffer pointer and calls the loader again. The referenced files WEAPONS.SPR and WEAPONS1.SPR are the sprites being requested.

name: request_chest_sprite_load
description: Points a global at a shared buffer and calls the loader routine. The referenced file CHEST.SPR is the sprite requested.

name: forward_indexed_entry_to_loader
description: Reads a 32-bit entry from a table indexed by a word value, stores it in a global, and calls the loader routine.

name: request_skeleton_sprite_load
description: Points a global at a shared buffer and calls the loader routine. The referenced file SKELETON.SPR is the sprite requested.

name: request_bigpig_sprite_load
description: Points a global at a shared buffer and calls the loader routine. The referenced file BIGPIG.SPR is the sprite requested.

name: request_shield_sprite_load
description: Points a global at a shared buffer and calls the loader routine. The referenced file SHIELD.SPR is the sprite requested.

name: request_devil_sprite_load
description: Points a global at a shared buffer and calls the loader routine. The referenced file DEVIL.SPR is the sprite requested.

name: request_cerberus_sprite_load
description: Points a global at a shared buffer and calls the loader routine. The referenced file CERBERUS.SPR is the sprite requested.

name: compute_request_offset_from_memory
description: Calls the loader routine twice around a step that scales a value read from a fixed memory location and adds it to a request value.

name: request_spic_image_load
description: Calls two routines, stores three fixed words into a global, then points a global at a shared buffer and calls the loader several times. The referenced file SPIC.IFF is the image requested.

name: load_entry_with_mode_switch
description: Saves a counter, calls several routines, then looks up a table entry using the counter minus one and passes it to the loader with a fixed value. A routine slot is written to zero before that load and to one afterwards.

name: gather_plane_longwords_into_buffer
description: Copies longwords from a source block into a destination buffer, reading four rows spaced 2100 bytes apart for each column and advancing through the source in 168-byte steps.

name: repeat_routine_rows_until_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly across four entries per row, advancing the pointer 42 bytes after each row, and stops when the routine returns zero.

name: scan_forward_for_body_tag
description: Advances a pointer two bytes at a time until the longword it reads equals the four-character tag BODY, then returns with the pointer left at that position.

name: unpack_run_length_row
description: Decodes a PackBits-style stream into a 40-byte row: a positive count copies that many following literal bytes, a negative count repeats the next byte, and the value 128 is skipped.

name: replicate_pattern_across_bitplanes
description: Writes a ten-longword pattern into four planes spaced 2100 bytes apart for each of 200 rows, advancing 42 bytes per row. The first longword of each block comes from a separate value.

name: replicate_pattern_with_counted_rows
description: Writes the same ten-longword pattern into four planes, but the number of rows is taken from the caller's counter register instead of being fixed.

name: forward_call_to_inner_routine
description: Calls one other routine and returns, with no other work in the body.

name: toggle_two_buffer_addresses
description: Sets a pair of globals to two fixed addresses, choosing which address goes into which global based on whether the first global already holds one of them.

name: set_default_buffer_addresses
description: Stores two fixed buffer addresses into two globals.

name: wait_for_beam_position
description: Spins until a global holds minus 56, then enters an endless loop. The referenced beam position register shows it waits for a raster position.

name: store_split_buffer_address_table
description: Stores five buffer addresses, each computed as a base plus a fixed offset, into a pointer table as split high and low words. It also replaces the low nibble of a global with its inverse and copies that nibble into the high nibble.

name: shift_two_word_register_left
description: Shifts a 32-bit value held in two words left by one bit, taking the new low bit from a bit of a state byte, and stores the high byte of the result in a global.

name: repeat_steps_until_result_clears
description: Calls three routines, then repeatedly calls another routine with a fixed argument until a register reaches zero, and repeats the whole sequence while its return value is nonzero.

name: decrement_nonzero_digit_fields
description: Subtracts one unit from each of the three low four-bit fields of a 16-bit value that is pointed to by the caller, but only where that field is nonzero.

name: repeat_steps_with_two_pointers
description: Calls three routines, then repeatedly calls another routine with two pointer arguments until a register reaches zero, and repeats while its return value is nonzero.

name: step_digit_fields_toward_target
description: Compares the three low four-bit fields of one word with the matching fields of another and adds one unit to the second word's field wherever they differ.

name: set_blitter_control_defaults
description: Writes six fixed values to the blitter control and modulo registers, zeroing the modulo registers and loading the control registers with constant settings.

name: deinterleave_four_word_planes
description: Splits a stream of four-word groups into four separate planes, writing one word of each group to each plane, for 4000 groups.

name: interleave_planes_with_zero_padding
description: Writes groups of planar words from a source table into a destination grid with 48-word row strides, storing zero in the third word of each group. The outer loop runs for a caller-supplied number of blocks.

name: init_display_state_if_armed
description: If a dispatch slot is set, clears a 256-byte scratch block, copies three words from a table chosen by a flag word, stores pointers to the scratch block in state variables, and returns one. Otherwise it returns its input unchanged.

name: reset_state_buffer_and_pointers
description: If a dispatch slot is set, clears a 256-byte scratch block, copies table values chosen by a flag word into state variables, and stores pointers to the scratch block. It returns nothing.

name: arm_and_reset_counter
description: If a dispatch slot is set, writes 128 to a global, zeroes a counter, and calls one routine. It does nothing otherwise.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: countdown_and_dispatch_steps
description: If a dispatch slot is set, decrements a state byte. When the result is zero it calls one routine four times and writes 128 to a global; otherwise it stores the decremented value, zeroes a counter, and calls a routine.

name: call_routine_four_times
description: If a dispatch slot is set, calls one routine four times in a row.

name: relink_object_frame_pointer
description: When a per-object flag is set, clears it, looks up a pointer from a table chosen by a state index, stores that pointer and its first word into two per-object slots, and copies a word into a global.

name: store_object_pointer_and_flag
description: Loads a per-object pointer and stores it, with its first word, into two per-object slots. It copies a word into a global, sets a per-object flag when a status bit is set, and writes the register word into a third slot.

name: reset_idle_object_fields
description: When a per-object counter is below four, copies one state byte to another field, clears a third, sets a fourth to seven, and fills eight longword fields of a pointed-to record with blank values: four-byte runs of 128 followed by zeros.

name: store_word_through_indirect_slot
description: Writes the register word into the location that a pointer slot points to, at an offset given by the caller.

name: clamp_value_to_global_quarter
description: Limits a byte to a quarter of a global when that global is nonzero and the byte is at least that large. If a dispatch slot equals 13 and a flag is set, it instead uses one more than a stored byte, and the result is written into a record field.

name: advance_per_object_sequencer
description: Runs one step of a per-object sequencer: when a countdown expires it reloads it and writes alternating marker values into a table, ramps a byte gradually, toggles a phase bit between two values, and updates a 16-bit value from a lookup table.

name: reset_object_motion_fields
description: Copies one state byte to another field, clears a second, sets a third to seven, and fills eight longword fields of a pointed-to record with four-byte runs of 128 followed by zeros.

name: initialise_pointer_table_sequence
description: Saves two globals into fixed slots, toggles a flag bit, resets a routine slot and two globals, then writes a sequence of constant pointers into one table slot, calling routines between writes. It finishes with a countdown loop.

name: increase_global_by_1024
description: Adds 1024 to a global variable and returns.

name: store_default_parameter_block
description: Stores nine fixed default values into consecutive globals: a zero, the values 980, 79 and 40, and several minus-one and one sentinels.

name: loop_steps_until_countdown_ends
description: Sets a loop counter to three and clears a flag, then repeatedly calls several routines, exiting when a routine returns a negative value or when a flag and a countdown both reach their end conditions.

name: copy_list_entries_in_passes
description: Walks a list of signed words ending in minus one. For each entry it checks a flag and a status, then copies a block of bytes whose length comes from the entry, repeating the whole walk for four passes.

name: verify_table_checksum
description: Negates and sums 128 longwords from a fixed table, then returns zero when the total equals a stored reference value and minus one otherwise.

name: copy_nonzero_entries_until_end
description: Repeatedly calls a routine, then copies nonzero longwords from a record's table into an output list in reverse order while a chained value stays nonzero, and finally writes a minus-one terminator.

name: find_matching_table_record
description: Scans a table of fixed-size records, comparing each record's stored name bytes with a reference buffer. On a match it stores the record's first word and a longword into globals and returns zero; if the end-of-table marker is reached it returns minus one.

name: build_record_list_returning_status
description: Once, walks a table of words ending in minus one, calls a routine for each entry, and stores the result, a longword, and 30 bytes copied from a fixed source area into a record ending in minus one. If a status flag is raised it stops and returns the routine's last value; then it sets a done flag.

name: populate_record_list_from_table
description: Once, walks a table of words ending in minus one, calls a routine for each entry, and stores the result, a longword, and 30 bytes copied from a fixed source area into a record ending in minus one. It stops early when a status flag is raised, then sets a done flag.

name: copy_nonzero_words_into_list
description: Once, copies the nonzero words from a source table into an output list, skipping zeros, and ends the list with minus one.

name: copy_longword_block_when_ready
description: When not already done and a status check after a routine call passes, copies 128 longwords from one pointer to another and returns the remaining counter.

name: copy_longword_block_after_check
description: When not already done and a status check after a routine call passes, copies 128 longwords from one pointer to another.

name: update_global_status
description: Calls a routine and stores its result in a status global. If that result is non-negative, it calls two more routines and, when the second returns a nonzero value, stores that value in the status global instead.

name: divide_value_by_twenty_two
description: Stores a word argument in a global, then divides the byte value by 22, storing the quotient and remainder in globals. The remainder is reduced by 11 when it exceeds 10, and a flag records that case.

name: divide_value_by_twenty_two
description: Identical to its neighbour: stores a word argument in a global, divides the byte value by 22 into a quotient and remainder global, reduces the remainder by 11 when it exceeds 10, and records that case in a flag.

name: program_disk_read_registers
description: Programs the disk hardware for a read: writes a disk pointer, a sync word and a control value into the disk registers, sets a global to a fixed value, and enables the disk DMA with a transfer length of two.

name: poll_disk_transfer_completion
description: Repeats a disk transfer step while two stored positions differ. Each step writes a fixed transfer length and polls a status bit for up to 65,535 iterations; it returns zero once the bit appears, otherwise it runs one final routine.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two other routines in sequence and returns.

name: scan_table_until_routine_succeeds
description: Repeatedly finds the next record in a fixed table whose first word matches a counter, calls a routine with it, and increments the counter. It stops when that routine returns one and then returns zero.

name: interleave_clock_and_data_bits
description: Combines 128 longwords pairwise: each output longword takes its even bits from one source longword and places the even bits of a second source, 512 bytes further on, into the odd bit positions.

name: pack_bit_interleave_table_entries
description: Calls a routine, then for ten table entries combines two longword fields by interleaving their bits. It writes the high and low bytes of the low sixteen bits of the result into a per-entry table, advancing 16 bytes each time.

name: locate_sync_words_in_buffer
description: Scans a data buffer for the sync word and records up to ten positions in a table, backing up one word when the match is not exact. It stops at the end of the buffer.

name: step_drive_position_toward_target
description: Moves a stored position one step at a time toward a target, writing a direction pattern to a drive control port on each step and calling a routine. It returns minus one once the position exceeds 79.

name: poll_status_bit_then_reset
description: If a stored position differs from a second value, repeatedly calls two routines while bit four of a status byte stays set and a counter is nonzero, then resets the stored value to zero.

name: busy_wait_count_down
description: Spins by decrementing the register value until it reaches zero, then returns. It is a fixed timing delay.

name: clear_selected_control_bit
description: Ors a byte with the constant 125, clears one bit whose index comes from a stored value plus three, and writes the result to a global that drives a control port.

name: write_drive_control_until_ready
description: Builds a control-port byte by clearing one bit chosen by a stored index, then sets or clears bit two depending on a flag, and writes it to a global. It repeats the write and read until bit five is clear.

name: clear_control_bit_then_delay
description: Clears one control bit chosen by a stored index, waits while bit five stays set, then runs a fixed countdown delay.

name: fill_entries_with_stepped_values
description: Fills 128 three-word entries: the first two words are set to minus 128, and the third counts upward in steps of seven.

name: stub_no_decoded_body
description: The decompiler produced no body, so only the facts are known: the routine touches the raster position register and one other custom chip register. No behaviour is recovered from pseudo-code.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: fill_pointer_table_from_scan
description: Scans a 128-entry byte table for the next value above the previous one. When the scan ends, it fills a 31-entry pointer table, each pointer advancing by a stride read from the structure, then sets a flag and clears counters.

name: advance_audio_playback_tick
description: Advances a tick counter. On each tick period it copies pointer and length pairs for four audio channels into the audio hardware registers and advances a sample offset by sixteen, wrapping at a limit; otherwise it calls four routines.

name: fill_pointer_table_from_scan
description: Same scan-and-fill logic as its neighbour: finds the next larger byte value in a 128-entry table and fills a 31-entry pointer table with a stride from the structure, then sets a flag and clears counters.

name: reset_control_fields_to_defaults
description: Writes zero to four global control bytes and fifteen to a fifth. The facts list audio channel and DMA registers, but the decompiled body shows only these assignments.

name: program_audio_channels_and_dma
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because the decompiler timed out. From the facts alone, it writes the pointer and length registers of the four audio channels and the DMA control register, and calls four other routines.

name: lookup_twelve_bit_table_indices
description: For four 14-word entries of a source table, copies a word and a nibble-based byte into a record. When the nibble is nonzero it searches a 36-entry word table for the masked 12-bit value and stores the index where it matches.

name: mask_and_compare_word
description: Masks a word to its low twelve bits and stores it in a field, then clears a flag byte. It compares the masked value with a limit field: equal values clear the stored field, and a smaller value sets the flag byte.

name: dispatch_command_by_nibble
description: Interprets one command from a packed control word by its low nibble: it updates a stored value by a byte amount with clamping, steps a value, adds a table-driven scaled offset, or adjusts a counter with a ceiling of 64, then returns the updated word.

name: install_handlers_and_loop
description: Stores a set of handler routine addresses and two buffer pointers into globals, then walks a linked list of entries without an exit. Each enabled entry with a nonzero field triggers routine calls, and entry counters are decremented to fire further calls.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: allocate_memory_and_init_state
description: Sets a global to one and allocates memory through library calls. On any allocation failure it reports the out-of-memory message and returns zero; on success it derives several pointers and counters from a structure and returns a value.

name: open_keyboard_device_port
description: Finds the current task, registers a message port through an exec call, stores two port fields, then opens the keyboard device. It returns zero on failure, otherwise it passes the opened device to a routine and returns it.

name: call_four_routines_in_order
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns, with no other work in the body.

name: copy_mouse_movement_sample
description: Copies one global into another. The facts list the mouse-port movement register as touched, so the copied value is probably a mouse movement sample.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: initialise_display_pointers_and_buffers
description: Derives several buffer pointers from a structure field and fixed offsets, allocates two blocks through a library call, and zeroes four longwords of one block. It calls intuition library routines for screen and window setup and stores display limits of 319 by 199 with 80-wide defaults.

name: copy_block_and_restart_copper
description: Copies words from one buffer into another up to a fixed end address, sets several pointers past the copied block, then calls library routines that load the copper list pointer and restart the copper.

name: find_value_in_table
description: Searches a table of 16-bit values for the value in the input register and returns the number of entries stepped over, or minus one when nothing matches.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: apply_scaled_offsets_to_table
description: When the input index is non-negative, multiplies a 16-bit value from a structure by a scale factor, adds four table longwords as offsets, and stores each sum as high and low words into a destination table four entries apart.

name: write_marker_bytes_per_entry
description: Walks up to four entries of a value table, stopping at a value above 200. For each nonzero value it writes a marker character (one of two, chosen by a flag) followed by a byte of 15, stores a pointer and value into the entry, and ends with two minus-one bytes.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: call_indirect_function
description: Calls a graphics library routine through a pointer stored in a global, then returns the register value unchanged.

name: wait_until_status_bit_set
description: Spins until bit four of a status global becomes set, then returns.

name: wait_until_low_bit_set
description: Spins until the lowest bit of a status global is set, then returns the input register value unchanged. The facts list the vertical position register as touched.

name: run_steps_then_set_mask
description: Calls two other routines, then writes 16 to a global. The body itself writes only that global.

name: apply_scaled_offsets_for_records
description: For three records, reads a destination pointer and a 16-bit scale value, then for four consecutive table longwords writes the scaled sum as high and low words, four entries apart.

name: run_supervisor_call_sequence
description: Sets a flag bit, writes two fixed byte values through a pointer, calls four routines, then runs a supervisor-state call sequence with an OS library call through a pointer. The referenced name BLANC.SND is the sound file this sequence concerns.

name: execute_supervisor_call_sequence
description: Calls two routines, writes two constants to a global, calls an OS library routine through a pointer, restores a saved global, and makes a second library call. The facts list supervisor and user state switches around these calls.

name: reset_and_call_supervisor_pair
description: Clears a global, calls a library routine through a pointer, saves a global, then calls a second library routine with the saved value.

name: call_pair_with_saved_value
description: Calls one library routine through a pointer, restores a previously saved global, and calls a second library routine with it.

name: increment_counter_then_call_seven
description: Increments a 32-bit counter, calls one routine four times, then calls three more routines. The register pair is returned unchanged.

name: countdown_channel_and_set_flags
description: If the guard global is zero and a per-index record's active byte and countdown byte are set, decrements the countdown. When it reaches zero, it sets a bit in two mask globals and, when a stored word is nonzero and a flag byte is negative, sets a further bit.

name: countdown_channel_flags_without_guard
description: Same countdown logic as its neighbour but without the guard check: when a per-index record's active byte and countdown byte are set, it decrements the countdown and on zero sets bits in two mask globals, plus a further bit when a stored word is nonzero and a flag byte is negative.

name: load_audio_channel_from_record
description: When the guard global is clear and a record's status byte is nonnegative, it either sets a channel bit (status zero) or loads the record's fields: a period value, a pointer and a length are written to the audio channel registers and a channel bit is set.

name: load_audio_channel_from_record
description: Same logic as its neighbour, without the guard check: when a record's status byte is nonnegative, it either sets a channel bit (status zero) or writes the record's period, pointer and length into the audio channel registers and sets a channel bit.

name: load_audio_channel_by_index
description: Takes a flag byte and an index from registers. It derives a period value, a length and a pointer-related value from the flag, writes them into the audio channel registers for that index, and sets a channel bit in a global mask.

name: update_audio_channel_period
description: Compares a register byte with a stored byte for an index. When they match it updates the stored count and writes a period value to the audio channel register; otherwise it stores the byte, sets an active flag, writes a fixed length of 1000, and sets a channel bit.

name: write_paired_registers_indexed
description: Writes one word into a global array slot selected by an index and another word into the audio channel register at the same index offset, then sets a bit in a global mask derived from a bit index.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns. The referenced name MAIN.AO is not used in its body.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: decode_tagged_record_buffers
description: When bit zero of a flag global is set, walks a list of records and, for tagged records, copies words into a destination laid out in 40-byte rows, 200 rows per pass. It then decodes a byte stream by splitting each byte into nibbles, looking each up in a table and adding a running value, and ends the output with two zero bytes.

name: expand_bitplane_records
description: Walks a linked list of records of two types, copying each record's data into four destination planes in 40-byte rows or, in the other branch, gathering one bit per plane from four source streams. The listing is truncated, so only these branches are described.

name: return_constant_3000
description: Returns the fixed value 3000 and does nothing else.

name: replicate_global_byte
description: Returns a 16-bit word made from the global byte repeated in both halves. The facts list timer registers as touched, but the body reads only the global.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns. The facts count more instructions than the empty body shows, so the listing may be incomplete.

name: copy_pointer_list_blocks
description: Walks up to four pointer pairs, stopping at a null source pointer, and copies a block of 16 words from each source to its destination. The first pair copies 32 words.

name: call_routine_then_write_pixel
description: Calls another routine, then calls the graphics library pixel-writing routine through a pointer, and returns the register pair unchanged.

name: call_draw_and_move
description: Calls another routine, then calls the graphics library Draw routine and then Move through pointers stored in a global, and returns.

name: call_rectfill_after_routine
description: Calls another routine, then calls the graphics library RectFill routine through a pointer, and returns the register pair unchanged.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: store_byte_and_set_pen
description: Stores the low byte of the register value in a global, calls the graphics library SetAPen routine through a pointer, and returns the register value.

name: set_background_pen_from_byte
description: Stores the low byte of the register value in a global, calls the graphics library SetBPen routine through a pointer, and returns the register value.

name: set_draw_mode_from_value
description: Maps the input value 3 to 4 and leaves other values unchanged, stores the result in a global, calls the graphics library SetDrMd routine through a pointer, and returns the original input.

name: poll_until_nonzero_then_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until its low byte is nonzero, then calls another repeatedly until it returns zero, and returns the first result.

name: draw_character_with_wrap
description: Handles one character: a carriage return advances a position by eight and a line feed resets a counter. Any other character wraps the column counter at 360, is stored in a global, is drawn through graphics library routines, and advances the column by nine.

name: call_routine_for_each_char
description: Walks a null-terminated byte string, calling another routine once for each nonzero byte, and returns zero.

name: clamp_and_scale_two_values
description: Clamps the first register value to at most 39 and the second to at most 24, then stores the first multiplied by nine and the second multiplied by eight in two globals.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: clamp_position_pair_to_limits
description: Sets a global to zero, adds a delta derived from it to two position values, clamps them to the ranges 0 to 639 and 0 to 399, and stores the masked bits of a global. The facts list mouse and joystick movement registers, which the body does not read directly.

name: double_two_input_values
description: Doubles the two 16-bit input values and stores them in two globals.

name: get_half_of_global
description: Returns a stored value shifted right by one bit. The facts list button registers as touched, but the body reads only the global.

name: find_first_differing_state_bit
description: Compares twelve pairs of state bytes and, on the first differing pair whose combined bit index is below 96, looks up a value, stores it in a global, copies three state values and returns. If no suitable pair is found, it clears the second set of twelve bytes.

name: map_status_flags_to_global
description: Calls an exec library I/O routine through a pointer, then builds a status global from bits of a flag byte, mapping each source bit to a fixed output bit.

name: compose_state_bits_into_result
description: Composes a return value from bits of a state global: the low byte gets bits chosen by the state's flags, and bit 128 is set when the state is nonnegative. The facts list the fire button register, which the body does not read.

name: compose_bits_from_d2_sign
description: Composes the same low-byte bits as its neighbour, but sets bit 128 according to the sign of a value in another register rather than the state global. The facts list the mouse movement register.

name: compose_bits_from_stack_arg
description: Composes the same low-byte bits as its neighbour, with bit 128 set from the sign of a value in another register. The facts list the joystick movement register.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: call_dos_open_map_zero
description: Calls a DOS library routine through a pointer and returns its result, replacing a zero result with minus one.

name: return_zero
description: Returns zero and does nothing else.

name: lock_and_unlock_conditionally
description: Calls a DOS library routine through a pointer and, when it returns a nonzero result, calls the paired unlock routine with the register argument.

name: close_and_optionally_reopen
description: Calls a DOS routine through a pointer and, when a global flag byte is nonzero, calls two further DOS routines and then loops forever. The referenced name BLANC.SND is the file involved.

name: call_routine_then_dos_open
description: Calls one routine, then calls the DOS library Open routine through a pointer and returns its result, replacing a zero result with minus one.

name: open_file_or_fail
description: Calls one routine, then calls the DOS library Open routine through a pointer. A zero result becomes minus one, and any other result is returned.

name: call_dos_read
description: Calls the DOS library Read routine through a pointer and returns nothing.

name: write_dos_then_set_flag
description: Calls one routine, then calls the DOS library Write routine through a pointer, and sets a global to one.

name: prompt_for_unprotected_disk
description: Waits for a status flag and a key code, then, unless the code is 82 or 81, calls several routines to show the prompt, waits for the return character and halts in an endless loop. The referenced text asks the user to unprotect the disk and press RETURN.

name: move_block_and_clear_source
description: Moves 18 rows of 20 groups from four source pointers into a destination buffer, four words per group, zeroing each source word after it is copied.

name: copy_block_back_to_planes
description: Copies 18 rows of 20 groups of four words from a source buffer back out to four destination pointers, without clearing the source.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty routine: it only returns, with no reads or writes.

name: wait_for_message_flag
description: Calls the exec GetMsg routine through a pointer. When a message has one of two flag bits set, it keeps polling until a message with flag bit fifteen appears, then returns.

name: return_stack_argument
description: Returns the value it was given on the stack, unchanged.

name: lock_and_set_current_dir
description: Calls the DOS Lock routine through a pointer. When the lock succeeds it stores the lock handle and makes it the current directory through a second DOS call; otherwise it calls two other routines.

name: call_two_routines_pass_through
description: Calls two other routines in turn and returns the stack argument unchanged. The referenced text 'error lock' is not used in this body.

name: return_zero
description: Returns zero and does nothing else.

name: wait_then_scale_difference
description: Waits until a status global is no longer minus one, then multiplies the difference of two globals by a stored word, divides by 1000, subtracts two from the quotient and clamps it at zero, returning quotient and remainder.

name: lock_and_query_volume_info
description: Locks a name through the DOS library, stores the lock, queries its information and unlocks it, returning minus one when the lock fails. The referenced device names DF0, DF1 and DH0 are the volumes it may name.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_when_needed
description: Picks a target from a flag. When it differs from the current buffer pointer, it saves five limit words, sets them to 0, 0, 319, 199 and 80, swaps two buffer pointers, restores the saved words, and calls routines around the swap.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_on_mismatch
description: Compares its register argument with a stored pointer and, when they differ, saves five limit words, sets them to 0, 0, 319, 199 and 80, swaps two buffer pointers, restores the words and calls routines. It returns the stack argument unchanged.

name: shift_buffer_rows_by_count
description: Shifts a row buffer by a count taken from a global: it copies a five-word pointer header, adjusts pointer and limit values by sixteen times the count, updates rows in a loop of count iterations, swaps two buffer pointers, then restores the saved limit words. The count is compared with 20.

name: add_offset_to_table_longs
description: Computes a value from a global by negating it and shifting it right three bits, adds that value to five consecutive longwords of a table, and calls another routine.

name: reset_limits_to_defaults
description: Sets five limit words to 0, 0, 319, 199 and 80, then calls a routine.

name: initialise_block_header_if_present
description: Calls a routine that returns a block pointer. If the pointer is null it clears a global; otherwise it computes row sizes and offsets from several globals, writes a header with a fixed word and two differences, and stores the block pointer.

name: write_block_header_for_pointer
description: Computes a row size from a structure field and derives sequential offsets and sizes from globals. It stores the input pointer, writes a fixed word and two differences into the block header, and returns the stack argument.

name: allocate_from_top_region
description: Computes a block size from the input value by rounding and adding nine, subtracts it from a top pointer, and if the result stays above a lower limit stores the size, moves the pointer and returns the block address. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: allocate_from_top_region
description: Same size-based allocation as its neighbour: subtracts a computed block size from a top pointer, returning the block address when it stays above a lower limit, or zero otherwise.

name: allocate_from_top_region

name: check_word_in_range
description: Calls a routine for a 16-bit value and returns zero when the value lies strictly between 6528 and 6625, otherwise returns 65535.

name: return_constant_6576

name: store_input_and_call_six
description: Stores the address-register input in a global, calls six routines in sequence, and returns the value held in a data register unchanged.

name: save_state_and_set_adkcon
description: Saves three globals and a hardware register value into saved variables, then writes fixed control values to three globals and to the ADKCON register.
